issues.legal_issue: An exemption from court fees limited to the trial stage does not extend to a memorandum of appeal.
material_facts: The plaintiff paid the reduced court fee on the plaint under an exemption that applied to the trial stage.
The same reduced fee was paid on the memorandum of appeal, although a higher fee was payable on it.
issues.conclusion: The trial-stage exemption did not apply to the appeal, and the memorandum of appeal was insufficiently stamped.
issues.legal_principle: The exemption was specifically confined to the trial stage. The court rejected the contention that an appeal is a continuation of the suit for the purpose of extending that exemption.

predicates.civil_appeal: A party filed an appeal from a decision in a civil suit.
predicates.exemption_limited_to_trial_stage: The applicable court-fee exemption was confined to proceedings at the trial stage.
predicates.appellate_fee_underpaid: The fee paid on the memorandum of appeal was less than the fee payable for it.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal is filed with an underpaid fee and the relevant exemption is confined to the trial stage, the exemption does not apply to the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court must give an appellant an opportunity to make good a court-fee deficiency before dismissing an insufficiently stamped memorandum of appeal.
material_facts: The appellate court found that the fee paid on the memorandum of appeal was insufficient.
The appellate court dismissed the memorandum without first allowing the appellant time to pay the deficiency.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal was inappropriate because the appellant should have been given an opportunity to pay the deficient court fee within a time fixed by the court; dismissal could follow if the appellant failed to comply.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 107(2) and 149 of the Code of Civil Procedure, read with the procedure under Order VII applicable to suits, require an opportunity to make good a fee deficiency. Section 149 permits the court, in its discretion, to allow payment at any stage, after which the document has the same force and effect as if the fee had been paid initially. The court also relied on fairness of procedure.

predicates.civil_appeal: A party filed an appeal from a decision in a civil suit.
predicates.court_found_fee_deficient: The appellate court determined that the fee paid on the appeal document was insufficient.
predicates.court_dismissed_without_allowing_payment: The appellate court dismissed the appeal document without first allowing the appellant time to pay the deficiency.

issues.definition: If an appellate court finds a fee deficiency and dismisses the appeal document without allowing time to remedy it, the dismissal is improper.

issues.legal_issue: Costs may be imposed to compensate respondents where an appellant's negligence has drawn them into prolonged proceedings.
material_facts: The appellants negligently failed to pay the proper fee on the memorandum of appeal.
The respondents had been drawn into proceedings that had continued for about ten years.
issues.conclusion: The appeal's restoration on payment of the proper court fee was made subject to payment of costs to the respondents.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated the appellants' negligence and the prolonged proceedings imposed on the respondents as grounds for compensatory costs.

predicates.civil_appeal: A party filed an appeal from a decision in a civil suit.
predicates.appellant_negligence: The appellant negligently failed to take a required step in the appeal proceedings.
predicates.respondents_drawn_into_prolonged_proceed: The respondents were required to participate in proceedings that continued for a prolonged period.

issues.definition: When an appellant's negligence draws respondents into prolonged proceedings, the respondents are awarded compensatory costs.
